title: Mixing Depth in Sparse Transformer FFN Layers: code and 326 training runs
description:
Code, raw experimental records, and analysis for a controlled study of structured sparsity in Transformer feed-forward layers under an equal-parameter and equal-FLOP constraint.

Seven connectivity patterns (dense, ring, small-world, random, block-diagonal, mosaic, butterfly) are compared across four densities and four depths. Per-layer coverage is shown to be an insufficient predictor of quality (two patterns with identical coverage differ by 9.6 sigma). The repository introduces the mixing depth tau, the number of layers a topology needs before every output can reach every input, computed from the binary masks alone. Tau was validated with two predictions registered in the experiment scripts before the corresponding runs were queued: freezing the butterfly's stage drops its quality onto block-diagonal (landing within 0.14 sigma), and in the sparsest regime butterfly overtakes ring despite half the coverage (by 2.53 sigma).

Includes all 326 raw run records as JSON, the SLURM scripts documenting each experimental grid, and analysis code that regenerates every number in the paper from the raw results. All runs were performed on NVIDIA H200 GPUs at TUBITAK ULAKBIM TRUBA.
